To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The probability that an observation of an in-control provider will fall outside either limit depends on the interpolation method used.

different interpolation methods can be used to calculate the probability characteristics of control limits in a funnel plot, and these methods can lead to different probabilities for an in-control provider falling outside the limits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the probability characteristics of funnel plot control limits.
the use of funnel plots to monitor and compare clinical outcomes between healthcare units.
the specification of control limits in funnel plots, and the probability of an ‘incontrol’ provider falling outside the control limits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of different interpolation techniques can lead to different conclusions.

the probability of the SMR of an ‘in- control’ provider falling beyond the upper or lower control limits of a funnel plot is always less than p for method 1, always greater than or equal to p for method 3, and can be either less than p or greater than p for method 2.
the probability of a provider falling outside the limits is greater than, or possibly equal to, the nominal probability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is not possible for an interpolation method to ensure that the probability that an observation of an in-control provider falls outside either limit is exactly p.
the probability of a provider being identified as an outlier is dependent on the method of interpolation.
the first interpolation method should be used for the calculation of control limits for funnel plots.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the probability that an observation of an in-control provider falls outside of the limits is not a constant, but is dependent on both the interpolation method and the expected number of observed events.
the probability of falling outside the limits depends on the interpolation method used.
users of funnel plot control limits must be aware of the potential differences between the methods, and specify the interpolation method they intend to use prior to any analysis.
